“How is the new curriculum selling?” Sandra asked, wrapping her hands around her mug of coffee.

“It’s slow,” Abby answered. “I need to do more advertising, but now that the product is finished, I find it difficult to promote.”

“What’s wrong?” Sandra asked. Abby had spent years developing a curriculum for special needs children. Her passion and dedication to the project was amazing, but now her zeal seemed stifled.

“Well,” Abby said slowly. “I feel like my co-worker constantly criticizes me. ‘The cover design is tacky, there is a misspelling on page 11’, I should have said this, this, and this. My project advisor wants me to work on advertising, but every time I move forward, she tells me I did something wrong.”

“Does it feel like jealousy?” Sandra asked.

“I hadn’t thought of that. I’m staying in the background, but that’s not helping. I feel crippled and I don’t know what to do.”

Sandra nodded. “It’s difficult to be the recipient of another person’s jealousy. But it’s worse to be the one who’s jealous. I’ve been there. It’s miserable.”

“How did you work through it?” Abby asked. “You don’t seem like a jealous person now.”

“It was one point in a message,” Sandra answered. “The minister said, ‘If you feel critical toward someone who is rejoicing, likely you are struggling with jealousy.’ I don’t remember anything else he said,” Sandra chucked, “but, I knew he had identified my problem. I often found it hard to be happy for my peers. I didn’t realize jealousy was my root problem.”

“That makes sense,” replied Abby.

“It is harder for jealousy to take root if I face the negative thoughts right away,” Sandra replied. “It’s a battle worth fighting. I am happier when I can ‘rejoice with them that do rejoice,’ like the Bible says to do.”

“Maybe my co-worker is dealing with negative thoughts about the success more that feeling annoyed at me,” mused Abby.

“That’s likely true,” replied Sandra. “Aim to put her fears to rest so that you can work together productively. Don’t react to her behavior.”

Like Sandra, I too, have had critical thoughts when peers shared good news, or I noticed their accomplishments. Unless checked immediately, that tinge of jealousy keeps me from being happy for others.

The Bible describes the brutality of envy and jealousy. Jealousy is as cruel as the grave. (see Song of Solomon 8:6). Envy [is] the rottenness of the bones –Proverbs 14:30. And, Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy? –Proverbs 27:4. Jealousy is extremely subtle. It can be covered with an aura of godliness. Not only does it have the potential to destroy my relationships now, but also those of my children and grandchildren.

Women don’t decide to be jealous. They don’t say, “Today I’m going to be jealous.” Often, it’s hard to pinpoint when jealousy enters the heart, or even if it is there. But if it is hard to be happy for others, maybe it’s time to search our souls. We are prepared to fight against jealousy when we understand how and where jealousy thrives—within the heart of each of us.

Peers Test Our Rejoicing

Generally, we aren’t envious of people that we’re not close to. Women all around the world get married, have babies, or move into a new house, and we scarcely notice. But it’s hard to rejoice when those near us in time, place, age, or reputation enjoy blessings that we wish for. More than once, a jubilant phone call announcing a milestone challenged my resolve to rejoice with a rejoicing friend. God understands the struggle and He leads me to rest and acceptance.

Recognize Jealousy

The definition of jealous is: ‘Feeling or showing envy of someone or their achievements and advantages.’ Jealousy pops up in many ways, such as craving to copy a peer. Jealousy belittles the achievements of another and tries to control the way others think of that person. Jealousy gloats about the distresses and failures of others, while basking in a spiritual bubble. Jealous people keep the rumor mill in full production by feeding it twisted truths.

Safeguard Your Thoughts

Jealousy starts in the mind. Dwelling on a suspicion or envying another person distorts truth. This is dangerous, because what you perceive as a truth, is a lie.

We decide someone is proud because they brought a beautiful dessert to a potluck. Or we think a sister is a negligent homemaker because she visited a woman at a nursing home. Why? We tend to judge others by our own motives. Isn’t it feelings of guilt, self-justification, or envy that cause us to heap a negligent title on someone who is visiting the elderly? We don’t know how long she thought about that visit or how her husband made it possible. Divisive thoughts converted into words wreak havoc among godly women. It causes extra work for church leaders and stunts the growth of a body of believers.

Embrace The Thought: “Life Isn’t Fair”

Sometimes someone will have something you desire. On the flipside, there are times you will have something another woman wishes for. “Life isn’t fair” is a fact of life that we cannot change; we can only adjust our attitude.

There were friends in the same church who each had a daughter of dating age. As life would have it, one daughter dated and married long before the other one began a courtship. The mother of the single girl determined that she would rejoice with her friend and her daughter. As a result, the mothers are still friends, the girls are friends, and it’s likely their children will be friends.

Count Your Own Blessings

Looking at the blessings of others and making comparisons makes it difficult to be happy and satisfied. The Apostle Paul warns of this: …but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise –2 Corinthians 10:12. Happiness will not come to women who neglect to appreciate what they already have. Neither will they happily rejoice with those who rejoice.

Know Who You Are In Christ

Jealousy stems from feelings of fear and insecurity. God created you for His honor and glory. There isn’t a need for competition, rather we ought to be content in knowing who we are in Jesus. For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them –Ephesians 2:8-10.

Have Friends, Not Rivals

We might hesitate to admit that we have a rival, but that’s what a friend will become if we aren’t able to celebrate the blessings in her life. Pray for her regularly, asking God to bless her. Letting go of suspicion and doing something nice for her will help dissipate the negative feelings you have developed.

The Scripture is clear about enmity toward our brother (or sister): He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now. He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him. But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes –1 John 2:9-11.

Replace Jealousy With Gratitude And Contentment

Negative thoughts come without invitation, but we can decide if they will stay or leave. Learn to redirect your attention to truth. Philippians gives us an excellent blueprint: Finally, brethren [sisters], whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things –Philippians 4:8.

When we are at peace with God, with ourselves, and with our fellow women, we will be content with our abilities and with the circumstances in which God has placed us. With our focus on God, we will find joy and the power to rejoice with them that rejoice.

«Как продаётся новая учебная программа?» — спросила Сандра, обхватив ладонями кружку кофе.

«Пока медленно, — ответила Эбби. — Мне нужно активнее её рекламировать, но теперь, когда продукт готов, мне трудно его продвигать».

«Что случилось?» — спросила Сандра. Эбби несколько лет разрабатывала учебную программу для детей с особыми потребностями. Её увлечённость и преданность делу были поразительными, но теперь её рвение, казалось, угасло.

«Ну, — медленно произнесла Эбби. — Мне кажется, что коллега постоянно меня критикует. „Дизайн обложки безвкусный, на странице 11 опечатка“, и так далее: надо было сказать то, это и ещё вот это. Мой консультант по проекту хочет, чтобы я занялась рекламой, но каждый раз, когда я делаю шаг вперёд, она говорит, что я что-то сделала не так».

«Тебе кажется, что это ревность?» — спросила Сандра.

«Я об этом не думала. Я держусь в тени, но это не помогает. Я чувствую себя беспомощной и не знаю, что делать».

Сандра кивнула. «Тяжело, когда кто-то завидует тебе. Но ещё хуже самому завидовать. Я через это проходила. Это ужасное чувство».

«Как тебе удалось с этим справиться? — спросила Эбби. — Сейчас ты не кажешься завистливой».

«Это была одна мысль из проповеди, — ответила Сандра. — Проповедник сказал: „Если ты критически относишься к тому, кто радуется, скорее всего, ты борешься с завистью“. Больше я не помню ничего из его слов, — усмехнулась Сандра, — но поняла, что он указал на мою проблему. Мне часто было трудно радоваться за ровесников. Я не понимала, что корень проблемы — зависть».

«Теперь понятно», — ответила Эбби.

«Зависти труднее укорениться, если сразу противостоять негативным мыслям, — сказала Сандра. — За эту борьбу стоит взяться. Я счастливее, когда могу „радоваться с радующимися“, как учит Библия».

«Возможно, коллега борется с негативными мыслями об успехе больше, чем просто раздражается на меня», — задумчиво сказала Эбби.

«Скорее всего, так и есть, — ответила Сандра. — Постарайся развеять её опасения, чтобы вы могли плодотворно работать вместе. Не реагируй на её поведение».

Как и Сандра, я тоже ловила себя на критических мыслях, когда ровесницы делились хорошими новостями или я замечала их достижения. Если сразу не дать отпор этому чувству, даже лёгкая зависть мешает мне радоваться за других.

Библия говорит о жестокости зависти. Ревность жестока, как преисподняя (см. Песнь песней 8:6). «Зависть — гниль для костей» — Притчи 14:30. И ещё: «Жесток гнев, неукротима ярость; но кто устоит против ревности?» — Притчи 27:4. Зависть чрезвычайно коварна. Она может скрываться за ореолом благочестия. Она способна разрушить не только мои нынешние отношения, но и отношения моих детей и внуков.

Женщины не решают завидовать. Они не говорят: «Сегодня я буду завидовать». Часто трудно определить, когда зависть входит в сердце и есть ли она там вообще. Но если нам трудно радоваться за других, возможно, пора заглянуть в свою душу. Мы готовы бороться с завистью, когда понимаем, как и где она укореняется, — в сердце каждой из нас.

Ровесницы испытывают нашу способность радоваться

Как правило, мы не завидуем тем, с кем не близки. Женщины по всему миру выходят замуж, рожают детей или переезжают в новый дом, а мы едва это замечаем. Но трудно радоваться, когда близкие нам по времени, месту, возрасту или положению люди получают благословения, о которых мечтаем мы. Не раз радостный звонок с сообщением о важном событии испытывал мою решимость радоваться вместе с подругой, которая радовалась. Бог понимает эту борьбу и ведёт меня к покою и принятию.

Распознайте зависть

Завистливый — это тот, кто «испытывает или проявляет зависть к кому-либо, его достижениям и преимуществам». Зависть проявляется по-разному, например в желании копировать ровесницу. Зависть принижает достижения другого человека и пытается влиять на то, что о нём думают окружающие. Зависть злорадствует над бедами и неудачами других, в то время как сама пребывает в духовном пузыре. Завистливые люди не дают иссякнуть сплетням, подпитывая их искажённой правдой.

Охраняйте свои мысли

Зависть начинается в уме. Если зацикливаться на подозрениях или завидовать другому человеку, правда искажается. Это опасно, потому что то, что вы принимаете за правду, — ложь.

Мы решаем, что кто-то гордится собой, потому что принёс на общую трапезу красивый десерт. Или думаем, что сестра пренебрегает домашними обязанностями, потому что навестила женщину в доме престарелых. Почему? Мы склонны судить о других по собственным мотивам. Разве не чувство вины, самооправдание или зависть заставляют нас навешивать ярлык «нерадивой хозяйки» на ту, кто навещает пожилых? Мы не знаем, как долго она думала об этом визите и как её муж помог ей его осуществить. Разобщающие мысли, высказанные вслух, сеют хаос среди благочестивых женщин. Это добавляет работы церковным руководителям и тормозит рост общины верующих.

Примите мысль: «Жизнь несправедлива»

Иногда у кого-то будет то, чего хотите вы. И наоборот: порой у вас будет то, о чём мечтает другая женщина. «Жизнь несправедлива» — это факт, который мы не можем изменить; мы можем лишь изменить своё отношение.

В одной церкви были подруги, у каждой из которых была дочь брачного возраста. Так сложилось, что одна дочь начала встречаться с молодым человеком и вышла замуж задолго до того, как другая вступила в отношения. Мать незамужней девушки решила, что будет радоваться за подругу и её дочь. В итоге матери до сих пор дружат, девушки дружат, и, вероятно, их дети тоже будут дружить.

Цените собственные благословения

Если смотреть на благословения других и сравнивать себя с ними, трудно быть счастливой и довольной. Апостол Павел предупреждает об этом: «…они, измеряя себя самими собою и сравнивая себя сами с собою, неразумны» — 2 Коринфянам 10:12. Женщины, которые не ценят то, что уже имеют, не обретут счастья. Не смогут они и радостно радоваться с радующимися.

Знайте, кто вы во Христе

Зависть возникает из чувства страха и неуверенности. Бог сотворил вас для Своей чести и славы. Не нужно соревноваться; напротив, нам следует довольствоваться тем, что мы знаем, кто мы в Иисусе. «Ибо благодатью вы спасены через веру, и сие не от вас, Божий дар: не от дел, чтобы никто не хвалился. Ибо мы — Его творение, созданы во Христе Иисусе на добрые дела, которые Бог предназначил нам исполнять» — Ефесянам 2:8–10.

Будьте подругами, а не соперницами

Возможно, нам неловко признать, что у нас есть соперница, но именно ею станет подруга, если мы не способны радоваться благословениям в её жизни. Регулярно молитесь о ней, прося Бога благословить её. Если отказаться от подозрений и сделать для неё что-нибудь приятное, это поможет рассеять возникшие у вас негативные чувства.

Писание ясно говорит о вражде к брату (или сестре): «Кто говорит, что он во свете, а ненавидит брата своего, тот ещё во тьме. Кто любит брата своего, тот пребывает во свете, и нет в нём соблазна. А кто ненавидит брата своего, тот находится во тьме, и во тьме ходит, и не знает, куда идёт, потому что тьма ослепила ему глаза» — 1 Иоанна 2:9–11.

Замените зависть благодарностью и довольством

Негативные мысли приходят без приглашения, но мы можем решить, останутся ли они или уйдут. Научитесь возвращать внимание к истине. Послание к Филиппийцам даёт нам прекрасный образец: «Наконец, братия [сёстры], что только истинно, что честно, что справедливо, что чисто, что любезно, что достославно, что только добродетель и похвала, о том помышляйте» — Филиппийцам 4:8.

Когда у нас мир с Богом, с собой и с другими женщинами, мы будем довольны своими способностями и обстоятельствами, в которые Бог нас поставил. Сосредоточив внимание на Боге, мы обретём радость и силу радоваться с радующимися.

“How is the new curriculum selling?” Sandra asked, wrapping her hands around her mug of coffee.

“It’s slow,” Abby answered. “I need to do more advertising, but now that the product is finished, I find it difficult to promote.”

“What’s wrong?” Sandra asked. Abby had spent years developing a curriculum for special needs children. Her passion and dedication to the project was amazing, but now her zeal seemed stifled.

“Well,” Abby said slowly. “I feel like my co-worker constantly criticizes me. ‘The cover design is tacky, there is a misspelling on page 11’, I should have said this, this, and this. My project advisor wants me to work on advertising, but every time I move forward, she tells me I did something wrong.”

“Does it feel like jealousy?” Sandra asked.

“I hadn’t thought of that. I’m staying in the background, but that’s not helping. I feel crippled and I don’t know what to do.”

Sandra nodded. “It’s difficult to be the recipient of another person’s jealousy. But it’s worse to be the one who’s jealous. I’ve been there. It’s miserable.”

“How did you work through it?” Abby asked. “You don’t seem like a jealous person now.”

“It was one point in a message,” Sandra answered. “The minister said, ‘If you feel critical toward someone who is rejoicing, likely you are struggling with jealousy.’ I don’t remember anything else he said,” Sandra chucked, “but, I knew he had identified my problem. I often found it hard to be happy for my peers. I didn’t realize jealousy was my root problem.”

“That makes sense,” replied Abby.

“It is harder for jealousy to take root if I face the negative thoughts right away,” Sandra replied. “It’s a battle worth fighting. I am happier when I can ‘rejoice with them that do rejoice,’ like the Bible says to do.”

“Maybe my co-worker is dealing with negative thoughts about the success more that feeling annoyed at me,” mused Abby.

“That’s likely true,” replied Sandra. “Aim to put her fears to rest so that you can work together productively. Don’t react to her behavior.”

Like Sandra, I too, have had critical thoughts when peers shared good news, or I noticed their accomplishments. Unless checked immediately, that tinge of jealousy keeps me from being happy for others.

The Bible describes the brutality of envy and jealousy. Jealousy is as cruel as the grave. (see Song of Solomon 8:6). Envy [is] the rottenness of the bones –Proverbs 14:30. And, Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy? –Proverbs 27:4. Jealousy is extremely subtle. It can be covered with an aura of godliness. Not only does it have the potential to destroy my relationships now, but also those of my children and grandchildren.

Women don’t decide to be jealous. They don’t say, “Today I’m going to be jealous.” Often, it’s hard to pinpoint when jealousy enters the heart, or even if it is there. But if it is hard to be happy for others, maybe it’s time to search our souls. We are prepared to fight against jealousy when we understand how and where jealousy thrives—within the heart of each of us.

Peers Test Our Rejoicing

Generally, we aren’t envious of people that we’re not close to. Women all around the world get married, have babies, or move into a new house, and we scarcely notice. But it’s hard to rejoice when those near us in time, place, age, or reputation enjoy blessings that we wish for. More than once, a jubilant phone call announcing a milestone challenged my resolve to rejoice with a rejoicing friend. God understands the struggle and He leads me to rest and acceptance.

Recognize Jealousy

The definition of jealous is: ‘Feeling or showing envy of someone or their achievements and advantages.’ Jealousy pops up in many ways, such as craving to copy a peer. Jealousy belittles the achievements of another and tries to control the way others think of that person. Jealousy gloats about the distresses and failures of others, while basking in a spiritual bubble. Jealous people keep the rumor mill in full production by feeding it twisted truths.

Safeguard Your Thoughts

Jealousy starts in the mind. Dwelling on a suspicion or envying another person distorts truth. This is dangerous, because what you perceive as a truth, is a lie.

We decide someone is proud because they brought a beautiful dessert to a potluck. Or we think a sister is a negligent homemaker because she visited a woman at a nursing home. Why? We tend to judge others by our own motives. Isn’t it feelings of guilt, self-justification, or envy that cause us to heap a negligent title on someone who is visiting the elderly? We don’t know how long she thought about that visit or how her husband made it possible. Divisive thoughts converted into words wreak havoc among godly women. It causes extra work for church leaders and stunts the growth of a body of believers.

Embrace The Thought: “Life Isn’t Fair”

Sometimes someone will have something you desire. On the flipside, there are times you will have something another woman wishes for. “Life isn’t fair” is a fact of life that we cannot change; we can only adjust our attitude.

There were friends in the same church who each had a daughter of dating age. As life would have it, one daughter dated and married long before the other one began a courtship. The mother of the single girl determined that she would rejoice with her friend and her daughter. As a result, the mothers are still friends, the girls are friends, and it’s likely their children will be friends.

Count Your Own Blessings

Looking at the blessings of others and making comparisons makes it difficult to be happy and satisfied. The Apostle Paul warns of this: …but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise –2 Corinthians 10:12. Happiness will not come to women who neglect to appreciate what they already have. Neither will they happily rejoice with those who rejoice.

Know Who You Are In Christ

Jealousy stems from feelings of fear and insecurity. God created you for His honor and glory. There isn’t a need for competition, rather we ought to be content in knowing who we are in Jesus. For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them –Ephesians 2:8-10.

Have Friends, Not Rivals

We might hesitate to admit that we have a rival, but that’s what a friend will become if we aren’t able to celebrate the blessings in her life. Pray for her regularly, asking God to bless her. Letting go of suspicion and doing something nice for her will help dissipate the negative feelings you have developed.

The Scripture is clear about enmity toward our brother (or sister): He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now. He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him. But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes –1 John 2:9-11.

Replace Jealousy With Gratitude And Contentment

Negative thoughts come without invitation, but we can decide if they will stay or leave. Learn to redirect your attention to truth. Philippians gives us an excellent blueprint: Finally, brethren [sisters], whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things –Philippians 4:8.

When we are at peace with God, with ourselves, and with our fellow women, we will be content with our abilities and with the circumstances in which God has placed us. With our focus on God, we will find joy and the power to rejoice with them that rejoice.

’’نیا نصاب کیسا فروخت ہو رہا ہے؟‘‘ سینڈرا نے کافی کا مگ دونوں ہاتھوں میں تھامتے ہوئے پوچھا۔

’’رفتار سست ہے،‘‘ ایبی نے جواب دیا۔ ’’مجھے مزید تشہیر کرنی چاہیے، لیکن اب جب کہ پروڈکٹ مکمل ہو چکی ہے، مجھے اس کی تشہیر کرنا مشکل لگتا ہے۔‘‘

’’کیا مسئلہ ہے؟‘‘ سینڈرا نے پوچھا۔ ایبی نے خصوصی ضروریات رکھنے والے بچوں کے لیے نصاب تیار کرنے میں برسوں لگائے تھے۔ اس منصوبے کے لیے اس کا جذبہ اور لگن حیرت انگیز تھی، لیکن اب اس کا جوش دبا ہوا محسوس ہوتا تھا۔

’’بات یہ ہے،‘‘ ایبی نے آہستہ سے کہا۔ ’’مجھے لگتا ہے کہ میری ساتھی کارکن مسلسل مجھ پر تنقید کرتی ہے۔ ’سرورق کا ڈیزائن بھدا ہے، صفحہ 11 پر املا کی غلطی ہے،‘ مجھے یہ، یہ اور یہ کہنا چاہیے تھا۔ میری پروجیکٹ مشیر چاہتی ہیں کہ میں تشہیر پر کام کروں، لیکن جب بھی میں آگے بڑھتی ہوں، وہ کہتی ہیں کہ میں نے کچھ غلط کیا ہے۔‘‘

’’کیا یہ حسد جیسا محسوس ہوتا ہے؟‘‘ سینڈرا نے پوچھا۔

’’میں نے اس بارے میں نہیں سوچا تھا۔ میں پس منظر میں رہ رہی ہوں، لیکن اس سے کوئی مدد نہیں مل رہی۔ مجھے لگتا ہے جیسے میں مفلوج ہو گئی ہوں اور مجھے سمجھ نہیں آتا کہ کیا کروں۔‘‘

سینڈرا نے سر ہلایا۔ ’’کسی دوسرے کے حسد کا نشانہ بننا مشکل ہوتا ہے۔ لیکن حسد کرنے والا ہونا اس سے بھی بدتر ہے۔ میں اس کیفیت سے گزر چکی ہوں۔ یہ بہت تکلیف دہ ہے۔‘‘

’’تم نے اس سے کیسے نمٹا؟‘‘ ایبی نے پوچھا۔ ’’اب تو تم حسد کرنے والی نہیں لگتیں۔‘‘

’’ایک پیغام میں ایک بات تھی،‘‘ سینڈرا نے جواب دیا۔ ’’واعظ نے کہا، ’اگر کسی کو خوشی مناتے دیکھ کر تم اس پر تنقید کرنے لگتی ہو، تو غالباً تم حسد سے نبرد آزما ہو۔‘ مجھے یاد نہیں کہ اس نے اور کیا کہا تھا،‘‘ سینڈرا ہنسی، ’’لیکن مجھے معلوم ہو گیا تھا کہ اس نے میرے مسئلے کی نشاندہی کر دی ہے۔ مجھے اکثر اپنے ہم عصروں کے لیے خوش ہونا مشکل لگتا تھا۔ مجھے احساس نہیں تھا کہ حسد ہی میرے مسئلے کی جڑ ہے۔‘‘

’’یہ بات سمجھ میں آتی ہے،‘‘ ایبی نے جواب دیا۔

’’اگر میں منفی خیالات کا فوراً سامنا کروں تو حسد کو جڑ پکڑنے کا موقع کم ملتا ہے،‘‘ سینڈرا نے جواب دیا۔ ’’یہ ایسی لڑائی ہے جسے لڑنا ضروری ہے۔ جب میں ’خوشی منانے والوں کے ساتھ خوشی مناتی‘ ہوں، جیسا کہ بائبل کہتی ہے، تو میں زیادہ خوش رہتی ہوں۔‘‘

’’شاید میری ساتھی کارکن کو میری وجہ سے جھنجھلاہٹ سے زیادہ، کامیابی کے بارے میں منفی خیالات سے نمٹنا پڑ رہا ہے،‘‘ ایبی نے سوچتے ہوئے کہا۔

’’غالباً ایسا ہی ہے،‘‘ سینڈرا نے جواب دیا۔ ’’اس کے خوف دور کرنے کی کوشش کرو تاکہ تم مل کر مؤثر طریقے سے کام کر سکو۔ اس کے رویے پر ردِعمل نہ دو۔‘‘

سینڈرا کی طرح، میں نے بھی اس وقت تنقیدی خیالات رکھے ہیں جب ہم عصروں نے خوش خبری سنائی، یا میں نے ان کی کامیابیاں دیکھیں۔ اگر حسد کی اس ہلکی سی لہر کو فوراً نہ روکا جائے تو یہ مجھے دوسروں کے لیے خوش ہونے سے محروم کر دیتی ہے۔

بائبل حسد اور رقابت کی سفاکی بیان کرتی ہے۔ حسد قبر کی مانند بے رحم ہے۔ (دیکھیے غزل الغزلات 8:6)۔ حسد ہڈیوں کو گلا دیتا ہے۔ — امثال 14:30۔ اور، قہر بے رحم ہے اور غضب طوفان کی مانند؛ لیکن حسد کے آگے کون ٹھہر سکتا ہے؟ — امثال 27:4۔ حسد نہایت باریک انداز میں چھپا رہتا ہے۔ اسے دینداری کے ہالے میں چھپایا جا سکتا ہے۔ یہ نہ صرف میرے موجودہ تعلقات تباہ کر سکتا ہے بلکہ میرے بچوں اور پوتے پوتیوں کے تعلقات کو بھی۔

عورتیں حسد کرنے کا فیصلہ نہیں کرتیں۔ وہ یہ نہیں کہتیں، ’’آج میں حسد کروں گی۔‘‘ اکثر یہ بتانا مشکل ہوتا ہے کہ حسد دل میں کب داخل ہوتا ہے، یا آیا وہ موجود بھی ہے۔ لیکن اگر دوسروں کے لیے خوش ہونا مشکل ہو تو شاید وقت آ گیا ہے کہ ہم اپنے دلوں کو ٹٹولیں۔ جب ہم سمجھ لیتے ہیں کہ حسد کیسے اور کہاں پروان چڑھتا ہے—ہم میں سے ہر ایک کے دل میں—تو ہم اس کے خلاف لڑنے کے لیے تیار ہوتے ہیں۔

ہم عصر ہماری خوشی منانے کی آزمائش کرتے ہیں

عموماً ہم ان لوگوں سے حسد نہیں کرتے جن کے ہم قریب نہیں ہوتے۔ دنیا بھر کی عورتیں شادی کرتی ہیں، بچے پیدا کرتی ہیں یا نئے گھر میں منتقل ہوتی ہیں، اور ہمیں شاذ ہی اس کا احساس ہوتا ہے۔ لیکن جب وقت، جگہ، عمر یا شہرت کے لحاظ سے ہمارے قریب لوگ وہ برکتیں پاتے ہیں جن کی ہم خواہش کرتے ہیں، تو ان کے ساتھ خوش ہونا مشکل ہوتا ہے۔ ایک سے زیادہ بار، کسی اہم موقع کا اعلان کرتی ہوئی پُرجوش فون کال نے خوشی منانے والی دوست کے ساتھ خوش ہونے کے میرے عزم کو آزمایا۔ خدا اس کشمکش کو سمجھتا ہے اور مجھے سکون اور قبولیت کی طرف رہنمائی کرتا ہے۔

حسد کو پہچانیے

حسد کرنے کا مطلب ہے: ’کسی شخص یا اس کی کامیابیوں اور فوائد پر رشک یا حسد محسوس کرنا یا ظاہر کرنا۔‘ حسد کئی صورتوں میں سامنے آتا ہے، مثلاً کسی ہم عمر کی نقل کرنے کی شدید خواہش۔ حسد دوسرے کی کامیابیوں کو گھٹاتا ہے اور یہ قابو پانے کی کوشش کرتا ہے کہ دوسرے لوگ اس شخص کے بارے میں کیا سوچیں۔ حسد دوسروں کی مصیبتوں اور ناکامیوں پر خوش ہوتا ہے، جبکہ خود کو ایک روحانی بلبلے میں محفوظ رکھتا ہے۔ حاسد لوگ توڑی مروڑی سچائیوں کے ذریعے افواہوں کی چکی کو مسلسل چلاتے رہتے ہیں۔

اپنے خیالات کی حفاظت کریں

حسد ذہن میں شروع ہوتا ہے۔ کسی شبہے پر غور کرتے رہنا یا کسی دوسرے شخص سے رشک کرنا حقیقت کو مسخ کر دیتا ہے۔ یہ خطرناک ہے، کیونکہ جسے تم حقیقت سمجھتی ہو، وہ جھوٹ ہے۔

ہم فیصلہ کر لیتے ہیں کہ کوئی مغرور ہے کیونکہ وہ اجتماعی دعوت میں ایک خوبصورت میٹھا پکوان لے کر آئی۔ یا ہم سمجھتے ہیں کہ ایک بہن گھر داری میں غفلت برتتی ہے کیونکہ وہ ایک نگہداشت گاہ میں کسی خاتون سے ملنے گئی۔ کیوں؟ ہم دوسروں کو اپنے ہی محرکات کے مطابق پرکھنے کی طرف مائل ہوتے ہیں۔ کیا احساسِ جرم، خود کو درست ثابت کرنا یا حسد ہی ہمیں کسی بزرگ سے ملنے والی عورت کو غفلت شعار کا لقب دینے پر آمادہ نہیں کرتے؟ ہمیں نہیں معلوم کہ اس نے اس ملاقات کے بارے میں کتنی دیر سوچا تھا یا اس کے شوہر نے اسے ممکن بنانے میں کیا کردار ادا کیا۔ تفرقہ ڈالنے والے خیالات جب الفاظ میں ڈھلتے ہیں تو دیندار عورتوں کے درمیان تباہی مچا دیتے ہیں۔ اس سے کلیسیا کے رہنماؤں کے لیے اضافی کام پیدا ہوتا ہے اور ایمانداروں کی جماعت کی ترقی رک جاتی ہے۔

اس خیال کو قبول کریں: ’’زندگی منصفانہ نہیں‘‘

کبھی کبھی کسی کے پاس وہ چیز ہوگی جس کی تم خواہش کرتی ہو۔ دوسری طرف، کبھی تمہارے پاس وہ چیز ہوگی جس کی کوئی دوسری عورت خواہش کرتی ہے۔ ’’زندگی منصفانہ نہیں‘‘ زندگی کی ایک ایسی حقیقت ہے جسے ہم بدل نہیں سکتے؛ ہم صرف اپنا رویہ بدل سکتے ہیں۔

ایک ہی کلیسیا میں ایسی سہیلیاں تھیں جن میں سے ہر ایک کی ایک بیٹی شادی کی عمر کو پہنچ چکی تھی۔ زندگی کے اتفاق سے، ایک بیٹی نے دوسری کے رشتۂ ازدواج میں بندھنے سے بہت پہلے ہی کسی سے ملنا شروع کر دیا اور شادی بھی کر لی۔ غیر شادی شدہ لڑکی کی ماں نے طے کیا کہ وہ اپنی سہیلی اور اس کی بیٹی کے ساتھ خوشی منائے گی۔ نتیجتاً مائیں اب بھی سہیلیاں ہیں، لڑکیاں سہیلیاں ہیں، اور غالباً ان کے بچے بھی سہیلیاں ہوں گے۔

اپنی برکتیں شمار کریں

دوسروں کی برکتوں کو دیکھنا اور موازنہ کرنا خوش اور مطمئن رہنا مشکل بنا دیتا ہے۔ پولس رسول اس سے خبردار کرتا ہے: …لیکن وہ اپنے آپ کو آپس میں ناپنے اور ایک دوسرے سے اپنا موازنہ کرنے والے نادان ہیں۔ — 2 کرنتھیوں 10:12۔ جو عورتیں اپنی موجودہ نعمتوں کی قدر نہیں کرتیں، وہ خوشی حاصل نہیں کر سکتیں۔ نہ ہی وہ خوشی منانے والوں کے ساتھ خوشی سے شریک ہوں گی۔

مسیح میں اپنی پہچان جانیں

حسد خوف اور عدم تحفظ کے احساسات سے جنم لیتا ہے۔ خدا نے تمہیں اپنے جلال اور عزت کے لیے پیدا کیا۔ مقابلے کی ضرورت نہیں؛ بلکہ ہمیں یہ جان کر مطمئن ہونا چاہیے کہ ہم یسوع میں کون ہیں۔ کیونکہ تمہیں ایمان کے وسیلے سے فضل ہی سے نجات ملی ہے، اور یہ تمہاری طرف سے نہیں، بلکہ خدا کی بخشش ہے؛ اور نہ اعمال کے سبب سے، تاکہ کوئی فخر نہ کرے۔ کیونکہ ہم اسی کی کاریگری ہیں، اور مسیح یسوع میں نیک کاموں کے لیے پیدا کیے گئے، جنہیں خدا نے پہلے سے ہمارے کرنے کے لیے تیار کیا۔ — افسیوں 2:8-10۔

حریف نہیں، سہیلیاں بنائیں

ہو سکتا ہے ہم یہ تسلیم کرنے سے ہچکچائیں کہ ہماری کوئی حریف ہے، لیکن اگر ہم اس کی زندگی کی برکتوں پر خوشی نہیں منا سکتے تو ہماری سہیلی حریف بن جائے گی۔ اس کے لیے باقاعدگی سے دعا کریں اور خدا سے درخواست کریں کہ وہ اسے برکت دے۔ شبہات چھوڑ دینا اور اس کے لیے کوئی اچھا کام کرنا تمہارے دل میں پیدا ہونے والے منفی احساسات کو کم کرنے میں مدد دے گا۔

اپنے بھائی (یا بہن) سے دشمنی کے بارے میں کلام واضح ہے: جو کوئی کہتا ہے کہ میں نور میں ہوں اور اپنے بھائی سے عداوت رکھتا ہے، وہ اب تک اندھیرے ہی میں ہے۔ جو اپنے بھائی سے محبت رکھتا ہے وہ نور میں رہتا ہے اور اس میں ٹھوکر کھانے کا کوئی سبب نہیں۔ مگر جو اپنے بھائی سے عداوت رکھتا ہے وہ اندھیرے میں ہے اور اندھیرے ہی میں چلتا ہے، اور نہیں جانتا کہ کہاں جاتا ہے، کیونکہ اندھیرے نے اس کی آنکھیں اندھی کر دی ہیں۔ — 1 یوحنا 2:9-11۔

حسد کی جگہ شکرگزاری اور قناعت اپنائیں

منفی خیالات بغیر بلائے آتے ہیں، لیکن ہم فیصلہ کر سکتے ہیں کہ وہ رہیں گے یا چلے جائیں گے۔ اپنی توجہ حقیقت کی طرف موڑنا سیکھیں۔ فلپیوں کا خط ہمیں ایک بہترین رہنما اصول دیتا ہے: غرض، بھائیو [اور بہنو]، جو باتیں سچی ہیں، جو باتیں شریف ہیں، جو باتیں راست ہیں، جو باتیں پاک ہیں، جو باتیں پسندیدہ ہیں، جو باتیں دل پسند ہیں، غرض جو نیکی اور تعریف کی باتیں ہیں، اُن پر غور کیا کرو۔ — فلپیوں 4:8۔

جب ہم خدا، اپنے آپ اور اپنی ساتھی عورتوں کے ساتھ صلح سے رہتے ہیں تو ہم اپنی صلاحیتوں اور اُن حالات پر قناعت کریں گے جن میں خدا نے ہمیں رکھا ہے۔ خدا پر توجہ مرکوز رکھنے سے ہمیں خوشی اور خوشی منانے والوں کے ساتھ خوش ہونے کی قوت ملے گی۔

“How is the new curriculum selling?” Sandra asked, wrapping her hands around her mug of coffee.

“It’s slow,” Abby answered. “I need to do more advertising, but now that the product is finished, I find it difficult to promote.”

“What’s wrong?” Sandra asked. Abby had spent years developing a curriculum for special needs children. Her passion and dedication to the project was amazing, but now her zeal seemed stifled.

“Well,” Abby said slowly. “I feel like my co-worker constantly criticizes me. ‘The cover design is tacky, there is a misspelling on page 11’, I should have said this, this, and this. My project advisor wants me to work on advertising, but every time I move forward, she tells me I did something wrong.”

“Does it feel like jealousy?” Sandra asked.

“I hadn’t thought of that. I’m staying in the background, but that’s not helping. I feel crippled and I don’t know what to do.”

Sandra nodded. “It’s difficult to be the recipient of another person’s jealousy. But it’s worse to be the one who’s jealous. I’ve been there. It’s miserable.”

“How did you work through it?” Abby asked. “You don’t seem like a jealous person now.”

“It was one point in a message,” Sandra answered. “The minister said, ‘If you feel critical toward someone who is rejoicing, likely you are struggling with jealousy.’ I don’t remember anything else he said,” Sandra chucked, “but, I knew he had identified my problem. I often found it hard to be happy for my peers. I didn’t realize jealousy was my root problem.”

“That makes sense,” replied Abby.

“It is harder for jealousy to take root if I face the negative thoughts right away,” Sandra replied. “It’s a battle worth fighting. I am happier when I can ‘rejoice with them that do rejoice,’ like the Bible says to do.”

“Maybe my co-worker is dealing with negative thoughts about the success more that feeling annoyed at me,” mused Abby.

“That’s likely true,” replied Sandra. “Aim to put her fears to rest so that you can work together productively. Don’t react to her behavior.”

Like Sandra, I too, have had critical thoughts when peers shared good news, or I noticed their accomplishments. Unless checked immediately, that tinge of jealousy keeps me from being happy for others.

The Bible describes the brutality of envy and jealousy. Jealousy is as cruel as the grave. (see Song of Solomon 8:6). Envy [is] the rottenness of the bones –Proverbs 14:30. And, Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy? –Proverbs 27:4. Jealousy is extremely subtle. It can be covered with an aura of godliness. Not only does it have the potential to destroy my relationships now, but also those of my children and grandchildren.

Women don’t decide to be jealous. They don’t say, “Today I’m going to be jealous.” Often, it’s hard to pinpoint when jealousy enters the heart, or even if it is there. But if it is hard to be happy for others, maybe it’s time to search our souls. We are prepared to fight against jealousy when we understand how and where jealousy thrives—within the heart of each of us.

Peers Test Our Rejoicing

Generally, we aren’t envious of people that we’re not close to. Women all around the world get married, have babies, or move into a new house, and we scarcely notice. But it’s hard to rejoice when those near us in time, place, age, or reputation enjoy blessings that we wish for. More than once, a jubilant phone call announcing a milestone challenged my resolve to rejoice with a rejoicing friend. God understands the struggle and He leads me to rest and acceptance.

Recognize Jealousy

The definition of jealous is: ‘Feeling or showing envy of someone or their achievements and advantages.’ Jealousy pops up in many ways, such as craving to copy a peer. Jealousy belittles the achievements of another and tries to control the way others think of that person. Jealousy gloats about the distresses and failures of others, while basking in a spiritual bubble. Jealous people keep the rumor mill in full production by feeding it twisted truths.

Safeguard Your Thoughts

Jealousy starts in the mind. Dwelling on a suspicion or envying another person distorts truth. This is dangerous, because what you perceive as a truth, is a lie.

We decide someone is proud because they brought a beautiful dessert to a potluck. Or we think a sister is a negligent homemaker because she visited a woman at a nursing home. Why? We tend to judge others by our own motives. Isn’t it feelings of guilt, self-justification, or envy that cause us to heap a negligent title on someone who is visiting the elderly? We don’t know how long she thought about that visit or how her husband made it possible. Divisive thoughts converted into words wreak havoc among godly women. It causes extra work for church leaders and stunts the growth of a body of believers.

Embrace The Thought: “Life Isn’t Fair”

Sometimes someone will have something you desire. On the flipside, there are times you will have something another woman wishes for. “Life isn’t fair” is a fact of life that we cannot change; we can only adjust our attitude.

There were friends in the same church who each had a daughter of dating age. As life would have it, one daughter dated and married long before the other one began a courtship. The mother of the single girl determined that she would rejoice with her friend and her daughter. As a result, the mothers are still friends, the girls are friends, and it’s likely their children will be friends.

Count Your Own Blessings

Looking at the blessings of others and making comparisons makes it difficult to be happy and satisfied. The Apostle Paul warns of this: …but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise –2 Corinthians 10:12. Happiness will not come to women who neglect to appreciate what they already have. Neither will they happily rejoice with those who rejoice.

Know Who You Are In Christ

Jealousy stems from feelings of fear and insecurity. God created you for His honor and glory. There isn’t a need for competition, rather we ought to be content in knowing who we are in Jesus. For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them –Ephesians 2:8-10.

Have Friends, Not Rivals

We might hesitate to admit that we have a rival, but that’s what a friend will become if we aren’t able to celebrate the blessings in her life. Pray for her regularly, asking God to bless her. Letting go of suspicion and doing something nice for her will help dissipate the negative feelings you have developed.

The Scripture is clear about enmity toward our brother (or sister): He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now. He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him. But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes –1 John 2:9-11.

Replace Jealousy With Gratitude And Contentment

Negative thoughts come without invitation, but we can decide if they will stay or leave. Learn to redirect your attention to truth. Philippians gives us an excellent blueprint: Finally, brethren [sisters], whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things –Philippians 4:8.

When we are at peace with God, with ourselves, and with our fellow women, we will be content with our abilities and with the circumstances in which God has placed us. With our focus on God, we will find joy and the power to rejoice with them that rejoice.

‘Hoe loopt het nieuwe lesprogramma?’ vroeg Sandra, terwijl ze haar handen om haar koffiemok sloeg.

‘Het gaat langzaam,’ antwoordde Abby. ‘Ik moet meer reclame maken, maar nu het product af is, vind ik het moeilijk om het te promoten.’

‘Wat is er aan de hand?’ vroeg Sandra. Abby had jarenlang gewerkt aan de ontwikkeling van een lesprogramma voor kinderen met speciale behoeften. Haar passie en toewijding aan het project waren indrukwekkend, maar nu leek haar enthousiasme te zijn gesmoord.

‘Nou,’ zei Abby langzaam. ‘Ik heb het gevoel dat mijn collega voortdurend kritiek op me heeft. “Het omslagontwerp is smakeloos, er staat een spelfout op pagina 11.” Ik had dit, dit en dat moeten zeggen. Mijn projectbegeleider wil dat ik aan de reclame werk, maar telkens als ik vooruitgang boek, zegt ze dat ik iets verkeerd heb gedaan.’

‘Voelt het als jaloezie?’ vroeg Sandra.

‘Daar had ik niet aan gedacht. Ik blijf op de achtergrond, maar dat helpt niet. Ik voel me verlamd en weet niet wat ik moet doen.’

Sandra knikte. ‘Het is moeilijk als iemand anders jaloers op je is. Maar het is nog erger om zelf jaloers te zijn. Ik heb het meegemaakt. Het is ellendig.’

‘Hoe ben je daar doorheen gekomen?’ vroeg Abby. ‘Je lijkt nu niet jaloers.’

‘Het was één punt in een preek,’ antwoordde Sandra. ‘De predikant zei: “Als je kritisch bent tegenover iemand die zich verheugt, worstel je waarschijnlijk met jaloezie.” Ik weet niet meer wat hij verder zei,’ lachte Sandra, ‘maar ik wist dat hij mijn probleem had benoemd. Ik vond het vaak moeilijk om blij te zijn voor mijn leeftijdgenoten. Ik besefte niet dat jaloezie het onderliggende probleem was.’

‘Dat klinkt logisch,’ antwoordde Abby.

‘Jaloezie krijgt minder makkelijk wortel als ik negatieve gedachten meteen onder ogen zie,’ antwoordde Sandra. ‘Het is een strijd die het waard is om te voeren. Ik ben gelukkiger wanneer ik “me verblijd met hen die zich verblijden”, zoals de Bijbel ons opdraagt.’

‘Misschien worstelt mijn collega met negatieve gedachten over het succes, in plaats van dat ze zich alleen maar aan mij ergert,’ bedacht Abby.

‘Dat is waarschijnlijk zo,’ antwoordde Sandra. ‘Probeer haar angsten weg te nemen, zodat jullie goed kunnen samenwerken. Reageer niet op haar gedrag.’

Net als Sandra heb ook ik kritische gedachten gehad wanneer leeftijdgenoten goed nieuws deelden of wanneer ik hun prestaties opmerkte. Als ik dat vleugje jaloezie niet meteen aanpak, weerhoudt het me ervan blij te zijn voor anderen.

De Bijbel beschrijft hoe wreed afgunst en jaloezie zijn. Jaloezie is zo wreed als het graf. (zie Hooglied 8:6). Afgunst [is] verrotting der beenderen – Spreuken 14:30. En: De grimmigheid is wreed, en de toorn is overstelpend; maar wie zal voor de nijdigheid bestaan? – Spreuken 27:4. Jaloezie is uiterst subtiel. Ze kan verhuld zijn onder een schijn van godsvrucht. Ze kan niet alleen mijn relaties nu vernietigen, maar ook die van mijn kinderen en kleinkinderen.

Vrouwen besluiten niet jaloers te zijn. Ze zeggen niet: ‘Vandaag ga ik jaloers zijn.’ Vaak is het moeilijk vast te stellen wanneer jaloezie het hart binnendringt, of zelfs of ze er wel is. Maar als het moeilijk is om blij te zijn voor anderen, is het misschien tijd om onszelf te onderzoeken. We zijn bereid de strijd tegen jaloezie aan te gaan wanneer we begrijpen hoe en waar jaloezie gedijt: in het hart van ieder van ons.

Leeftijdgenoten stellen ons vermogen tot blijdschap op de proef

Over het algemeen zijn we niet afgunstig op mensen met wie we niet close zijn. Overal ter wereld trouwen vrouwen, krijgen ze kinderen of verhuizen ze naar een nieuw huis, en wij merken het nauwelijks op. Maar het is moeilijk om blij te zijn wanneer mensen die qua tijd, plaats, leeftijd of reputatie dicht bij ons staan, zegeningen ontvangen waar wij naar verlangen. Meer dan eens stelde een uitgelaten telefoontje met de aankondiging van een mijlpaal mijn besluit op de proef om me te verblijden met een vriendin die zich verheugde. God begrijpt die worsteling en leidt me naar rust en aanvaarding.

Herken jaloezie

De definitie van jaloers is: ‘Afgunst voelen jegens iemand of diens prestaties en voordelen, of die afgunst tonen.’ Jaloezie komt op veel manieren naar boven, bijvoorbeeld doordat je ernaar verlangt een leeftijdgenoot na te doen. Jaloezie kleineert de prestaties van een ander en probeert te bepalen hoe anderen over die persoon denken. Jaloezie verheugt zich over de tegenslagen en mislukkingen van anderen, terwijl ze zich koestert in een geestelijke bubbel. Jaloerse mensen houden de geruchtenmolen draaiende door verdraaide waarheden te verspreiden.

Waak over je gedachten

Jaloezie begint in je gedachten. Als je blijft stilstaan bij een vermoeden of afgunstig bent op iemand anders, vervormt dat de waarheid. Dat is gevaarlijk, want wat jij voor waarheid houdt, is een leugen.

We besluiten dat iemand trots is omdat ze een prachtig dessert heeft meegenomen naar een gezamenlijke maaltijd. Of we denken dat een zuster haar huishouden verwaarloost omdat ze een vrouw in een verpleeghuis heeft bezocht. Waarom? We hebben de neiging anderen te beoordelen op grond van onze eigen motieven. Zijn het niet schuldgevoelens, zelfrechtvaardiging of afgunst die ons ertoe brengen iemand die ouderen bezoekt het etiket ‘verwaarlozend’ op te plakken? We weten niet hoelang ze over dat bezoek heeft nagedacht of hoe haar man het mogelijk heeft gemaakt. Verdeeldheid zaaiende gedachten die in woorden worden omgezet, richten grote schade aan onder godvrezende vrouwen. Ze bezorgen kerkleiders extra werk en remmen de groei van een gemeenschap van gelovigen.

Omarm de gedachte: ‘Het leven is niet eerlijk’

Soms heeft iemand iets wat jij graag zou willen hebben. Omgekeerd zijn er momenten waarop jij iets hebt waar een andere vrouw naar verlangt. ‘Het leven is niet eerlijk’ is een feit dat we niet kunnen veranderen; we kunnen alleen onze houding aanpassen.

Er waren vriendinnen in dezelfde kerk die allebei een dochter hadden die oud genoeg was om te daten. Zoals het leven soms loopt, kreeg de ene dochter een relatie en trouwde ze lang voordat de andere aan verkering begon. De moeder van het meisje dat nog vrijgezel was, besloot dat ze zich met haar vriendin en haar dochter zou verheugen. Daardoor zijn de moeders nog steeds vriendinnen, zijn de meisjes vriendinnen en zullen hun kinderen waarschijnlijk ook bevriend zijn.

Tel je eigen zegeningen

Als je naar de zegeningen van anderen kijkt en vergelijkingen maakt, wordt het moeilijk om gelukkig en tevreden te zijn. De apostel Paulus waarschuwt hiervoor: …maar zij, die zichzelf naar zichzelf afmeten, en zichzelf met zichzelf vergelijken, zijn onverstandig – 2 Korintiërs 10:12. Vrouwen die niet waarderen wat ze al hebben, zullen geen geluk vinden. Evenmin zullen zij zich met vreugde verblijden met hen die zich verblijden.

Weet wie je bent in Christus

Jaloezie komt voort uit gevoelens van angst en onzekerheid. God heeft je geschapen tot Zijn eer en heerlijkheid. Er is geen reden om met elkaar te wedijveren; we behoren er juist tevreden mee te zijn te weten wie we in Jezus zijn. Want uit genade zijt gij zalig geworden door het geloof; en dat niet uit u, het is Gods gave; niet uit de werken, opdat niemand roeme. Want wij zijn Zijn maaksel, geschapen in Christus Jezus tot goede werken, welke God voorbereid heeft, opdat wij daarin zouden wandelen – Efeziërs 2:8-10.

Wees vriendinnen, geen rivalen

Misschien aarzelen we toe te geven dat we een rivale hebben, maar dat is wat een vriendin zal worden als we de zegeningen in haar leven niet kunnen vieren. Bid regelmatig voor haar en vraag God haar te zegenen. Door je achterdocht los te laten en iets aardigs voor haar te doen, zullen de negatieve gevoelens die je hebt ontwikkeld afnemen.

De Schrift is duidelijk over vijandschap jegens onze broeder (of zuster): Wie zegt dat hij in het licht is en zijn broeder haat, is tot nu toe in de duisternis. Wie zijn broeder liefheeft, blijft in het licht, en er is in hem geen aanleiding tot struikelen. Maar wie zijn broeder haat, is in de duisternis en wandelt in de duisternis en weet niet waarheen hij gaat, omdat de duisternis zijn ogen verblind heeft – 1 Johannes 2:9-11.

Vervang jaloezie door dankbaarheid en tevredenheid

Negatieve gedachten komen ongevraagd op, maar we kunnen beslissen of we ze laten blijven of wegsturen. Leer je aandacht opnieuw op de waarheid te richten. Filippenzen geeft ons een uitstekend richtsnoer: Ten slotte, broeders [zusters], al wat waar is, al wat eerbaar is, al wat rechtvaardig is, al wat rein is, al wat lieflijk is, al wat welluidend is; als er enige deugd is en als er enige lof is, bedenk dat – Filippenzen 4:8.

Wanneer we in vrede leven met God, met onszelf en met onze medezusters, zullen we tevreden zijn met onze mogelijkheden en met de omstandigheden waarin God ons heeft geplaatst. Als we onze aandacht op God gericht houden, zullen we vreugde vinden en het vermogen om ons te verblijden met hen die zich verblijden.

“How is the new curriculum selling?” Sandra asked, wrapping her hands around her mug of coffee.

“It’s slow,” Abby answered. “I need to do more advertising, but now that the product is finished, I find it difficult to promote.”

“What’s wrong?” Sandra asked. Abby had spent years developing a curriculum for special needs children. Her passion and dedication to the project was amazing, but now her zeal seemed stifled.

“Well,” Abby said slowly. “I feel like my co-worker constantly criticizes me. ‘The cover design is tacky, there is a misspelling on page 11’, I should have said this, this, and this. My project advisor wants me to work on advertising, but every time I move forward, she tells me I did something wrong.”

“Does it feel like jealousy?” Sandra asked.

“I hadn’t thought of that. I’m staying in the background, but that’s not helping. I feel crippled and I don’t know what to do.”

Sandra nodded. “It’s difficult to be the recipient of another person’s jealousy. But it’s worse to be the one who’s jealous. I’ve been there. It’s miserable.”

“How did you work through it?” Abby asked. “You don’t seem like a jealous person now.”

“It was one point in a message,” Sandra answered. “The minister said, ‘If you feel critical toward someone who is rejoicing, likely you are struggling with jealousy.’ I don’t remember anything else he said,” Sandra chucked, “but, I knew he had identified my problem. I often found it hard to be happy for my peers. I didn’t realize jealousy was my root problem.”

“That makes sense,” replied Abby.

“It is harder for jealousy to take root if I face the negative thoughts right away,” Sandra replied. “It’s a battle worth fighting. I am happier when I can ‘rejoice with them that do rejoice,’ like the Bible says to do.”

“Maybe my co-worker is dealing with negative thoughts about the success more that feeling annoyed at me,” mused Abby.

“That’s likely true,” replied Sandra. “Aim to put her fears to rest so that you can work together productively. Don’t react to her behavior.”

The Bible describes the brutality of envy and jealousy. Jealousy is as cruel as the grave. (see Song of Solomon 8:6). Envy [is] the rottenness of the bones –Proverbs 14:30. And, Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy? –Proverbs 27:4. Jealousy is extremely subtle. It can be covered with an aura of godliness. Not only does it have the potential to destroy my relationships now, but also those of my children and grandchildren.

The definition of jealous is: ‘Feeling or showing envy of someone or their achievements and advantages.’ Jealousy pops up in many ways, such as craving to copy a peer. Jealousy belittles the achievements of another and tries to control the way others think of that person. Jealousy gloats about the distresses and failures of others, while basking in a spiritual bubble. Jealous people keep the rumor mill in full production by feeding it twisted truths.

Jealousy starts in the mind. Dwelling on a suspicion or envying another person distorts truth. This is dangerous, because what you perceive as a truth, is a lie.

We decide someone is proud because they brought a beautiful dessert to a potluck. Or we think a sister is a negligent homemaker because she visited a woman at a nursing home. Why? We tend to judge others by our own motives. Isn’t it feelings of guilt, self-justification, or envy that cause us to heap a negligent title on someone who is visiting the elderly? We don’t know how long she thought about that visit or how her husband made it possible. Divisive thoughts converted into words wreak havoc among godly women. It causes extra work for church leaders and stunts the growth of a body of believers.

Sometimes someone will have something you desire. On the flipside, there are times you will have something another woman wishes for. “Life isn’t fair” is a fact of life that we cannot change; we can only adjust our attitude.

There were friends in the same church who each had a daughter of dating age. As life would have it, one daughter dated and married long before the other one began a courtship. The mother of the single girl determined that she would rejoice with her friend and her daughter. As a result, the mothers are still friends, the girls are friends, and it’s likely their children will be friends.

Looking at the blessings of others and making comparisons makes it difficult to be happy and satisfied. The Apostle Paul warns of this: …but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise –2 Corinthians 10:12. Happiness will not come to women who neglect to appreciate what they already have. Neither will they happily rejoice with those who rejoice.

For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them –Ephesians 2:8-10.

—¿Cómo se está vendiendo el nuevo plan de estudios? —preguntó Sandra, rodeando su taza de café con las manos.

—Va lento —respondió Abby—. Necesito hacer más publicidad, pero ahora que el producto está terminado, me resulta difícil promocionarlo.

—¿Qué pasa? —preguntó Sandra. Abby había pasado años desarrollando un plan de estudios para niños con necesidades especiales. Su pasión y dedicación al proyecto eran admirables, pero ahora su entusiasmo parecía apagado.

—Bueno —dijo Abby despacio—. Siento que mi compañera de trabajo me critica constantemente. «El diseño de la portada es de mal gusto; hay un error ortográfico en la página 11». Debería haber dicho esto, aquello y lo otro. Mi asesora del proyecto quiere que trabaje en la publicidad, pero cada vez que avanzo, me dice que hice algo mal.

—¿Te parece que podría ser por celos? —preguntó Sandra.

—No lo había pensado. Me estoy quedando en segundo plano, pero eso no ayuda. Me siento paralizada y no sé qué hacer.

Sandra asintió. —Es difícil ser quien recibe los celos de otra persona. Pero es peor ser quien siente celos. Yo he pasado por eso. Es horrible.

—¿Cómo lograste superarlo? —preguntó Abby—. Ahora no pareces una persona celosa.

—Fue una de las ideas de un sermón —respondió Sandra—. El ministro dijo: «Si sientes una actitud crítica hacia alguien que se está alegrando, es probable que estés luchando contra los celos». No recuerdo qué más dijo —se rio Sandra—, pero supe que había identificado mi problema. A menudo me costaba alegrarme por mis compañeras. No me daba cuenta de que la raíz del problema eran los celos.

—Tiene sentido —respondió Abby.

—Es más difícil que los celos echen raíces si enfrento enseguida los pensamientos negativos —respondió Sandra—. Es una batalla que vale la pena librar. Soy más feliz cuando puedo «gozarme con los que se gozan», como dice la Biblia que debemos hacer.

—Quizás mi compañera de trabajo esté lidiando con pensamientos negativos sobre el éxito, más que sintiéndose molesta conmigo —reflexionó Abby.

—Probablemente sea así —respondió Sandra—. Trata de disipar sus temores para que puedan trabajar juntas de manera productiva. No reacciones a su comportamiento.

Al igual que Sandra, yo también he tenido pensamientos críticos cuando mis compañeras compartían buenas noticias o cuando me fijaba en sus logros. Si no freno enseguida esa pizca de celos, me impide alegrarme por los demás.

La Biblia describe la crueldad de la envidia y los celos. Los celos son crueles como el sepulcro. (véase Cantares 8:6). La envidia es carcoma de los huesos —Proverbios 14:30. Y cruel es la ira, e impetuoso el furor; mas ¿quién podrá sostenerse delante de la envidia? —Proverbios 27:4. Los celos son sumamente sutiles. Pueden ocultarse bajo un aura de piedad. No solo pueden destruir mis relaciones actuales, sino también las de mis hijos y nietos.

Las mujeres no deciden tener celos. No dicen: «Hoy voy a sentir celos». A menudo es difícil precisar cuándo entran los celos en el corazón, o incluso si están allí. Pero si nos cuesta alegrarnos por los demás, quizás sea hora de escudriñar nuestra alma. Estamos preparadas para luchar contra los celos cuando entendemos cómo y dónde prosperan: en el corazón de cada una de nosotras.

Las compañeras ponen a prueba nuestra capacidad de alegrarnos

Por lo general, no envidiamos a las personas con quienes no tenemos una relación cercana. Mujeres de todo el mundo se casan, tienen bebés o se mudan a una casa nueva, y apenas nos damos cuenta. Pero es difícil alegrarnos cuando quienes están cerca de nosotras por la época, el lugar, la edad o la reputación disfrutan de bendiciones que deseamos. Más de una vez, una llamada jubilosa que anunciaba un hito puso a prueba mi determinación de alegrarme con una amiga que se alegraba. Dios comprende la lucha y me guía a descansar y aceptar.

Reconoce los celos

La definición de celoso es: «Sentir o mostrar envidia de alguien, de sus logros o de sus ventajas». Los celos se manifiestan de muchas maneras, como el deseo de imitar a una compañera. Los celos menosprecian los logros de otra persona y tratan de controlar lo que los demás piensan de ella. Los celos se regodean en las angustias y los fracasos de los demás, mientras se recrean en una burbuja espiritual. Las personas celosas mantienen en plena actividad la maquinaria de los rumores al alimentarla con verdades tergiversadas.

Protege tus pensamientos

Los celos comienzan en la mente. Darle vueltas a una sospecha o envidiar a otra persona distorsiona la verdad. Esto es peligroso, porque lo que percibes como verdad es mentira.

Decidimos que alguien es orgullosa porque llevó un postre exquisito a una comida compartida. O pensamos que una hermana descuida su hogar porque visitó a una mujer en un hogar de ancianos. ¿Por qué? Tendemos a juzgar a los demás por nuestros propios motivos. ¿No son los sentimientos de culpa, la justificación propia o la envidia los que nos llevan a etiquetar de negligente a alguien que visita a los ancianos? No sabemos cuánto tiempo pensó en esa visita ni cómo su esposo hizo posible que fuera. Los pensamientos divisivos convertidos en palabras causan estragos entre las mujeres piadosas. Esto genera trabajo adicional para los líderes de la iglesia y frena el crecimiento de una comunidad de creyentes.

Acepta esta idea: «La vida no es justa»

A veces alguien tendrá algo que deseas. Por otro lado, habrá ocasiones en que tú tendrás algo que otra mujer desea. «La vida no es justa» es una realidad que no podemos cambiar; solo podemos ajustar nuestra actitud.

Había amigas de la misma iglesia que tenían, cada una, una hija en edad de empezar a salir con alguien. Como suele suceder, una hija empezó a salir con alguien y se casó mucho antes de que la otra comenzara un noviazgo. La madre de la joven soltera decidió que se alegraría con su amiga y con la hija de esta. Como resultado, las madres siguen siendo amigas, las jóvenes son amigas y es probable que sus hijos también sean amigos.

Cuenta tus propias bendiciones

Mirar las bendiciones de los demás y hacer comparaciones dificulta sentirse feliz y satisfecha. El apóstol Pablo nos advierte: …pero ellos, midiéndose a sí mismos por sí mismos, y comparándose consigo mismos, no son juiciosos —2 Corintios 10:12. Las mujeres que no aprecian lo que ya tienen no serán felices. Tampoco se alegrarán de corazón con los que se alegran.

Conoce quién eres en Cristo

Los celos nacen de sentimientos de temor e inseguridad. Dios te creó para su honra y gloria. No hay necesidad de competir; más bien, debemos estar satisfechas sabiendo quiénes somos en Jesús. Porque por gracia sois salvos por medio de la fe; y esto no de vosotros, pues es don de Dios; no por obras, para que nadie se gloríe. Porque somos hechura suya, creados en Cristo Jesús para buenas obras, las cuales Dios preparó de antemano para que anduviésemos en ellas —Efesios 2:8-10.

Ten amigas, no rivales

Quizás dudemos en admitir que tenemos una rival, pero eso es lo que una amiga llegará a ser si no somos capaces de celebrar las bendiciones de su vida. Ora por ella regularmente y pídele a Dios que la bendiga. Dejar de lado las sospechas y hacer algo amable por ella ayudará a disipar los sentimientos negativos que has desarrollado.

La Escritura es clara acerca de la enemistad hacia nuestro hermano (o hermana): El que dice que está en la luz, y aborrece a su hermano, está todavía en tinieblas. El que ama a su hermano, permanece en la luz, y en él no hay tropiezo. Pero el que aborrece a su hermano está en tinieblas, y anda en tinieblas, y no sabe a dónde va, porque las tinieblas le han cegado los ojos —1 Juan 2:9-11.

Reemplaza los celos con gratitud y contentamiento

Los pensamientos negativos llegan sin que los invitemos, pero podemos decidir si se quedan o se van. Aprende a dirigir tu atención hacia la verdad. Filipenses nos ofrece un excelente modelo: Por lo demás, hermanos [y hermanas], todo lo que es verdadero, todo lo honesto, todo lo justo, todo lo puro, todo lo amable, todo lo que es de buen nombre; si hay virtud alguna, si algo digno de alabanza, en esto pensad —Filipenses 4:8.

Cuando estemos en paz con Dios, con nosotras mismas y con las demás mujeres, estaremos satisfechas con nuestras capacidades y con las circunstancias en las que Dios nos ha puesto. Al centrar nuestra atención en Dios, encontraremos gozo y el poder de alegrarnos con los que se alegran.

Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father –Matthew 10:29.

Of all the many, various winged creatures that frequent the skies, the sparrow is certainly esteemed among the lowest. People usually regard these drab birds as noisy, troublesome, and way overabundant. The original sparrows native to North America are shy birds of the fields and meadows. They are neither abundant nor bothersome. But the birds with a dour reputation for being disagreeable are house sparrows, which are native to Europe. They were introduced to our shores in the nineteenth century and with no natural controls present, increased rapidly. These are the “sparrows” spoken of in the Bible.

The sparrows to which Jesus referred are the world’s best-known sparrow and belong to the weaver finch family, which includes nearly three-hundred different species. It adapts so well to human habitation that it rarely breeds very far from civilization. Instead of admiring the sparrow’s adaptability, we view it as a pest. This bird was not esteemed much higher in Christ’s day and two were sold for a farthing (about a half cent).

The poorest of the poor in Israel would arrive at the meat market and scan the display. Beef, lamb, and fish were priced out of their budget. One copper farthing would purchase two sparrows. If they were to place two coins on the counter, they would receive four birds. Then possibly they would stare into the eyes of the store owner: Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings… –Luke 12:6. Like the present day “baker’s dozen”, this typical scene had repeated itself so often that it had become tradition: the merchant would then produce an extra bird and present it to his patron for free.

As a little boy with poor parents, it is highly probable that in the days of Jesus’ young life this scene had repeated itself before His own eyes. The fifth sparrow, of no value, had been thrown into the deal as a measure of goodwill and grace. Yet, this sordid specimen did not fall on the ground without the notice of the divine Father. Thus, streamed out the sublime and benedictory words, But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows –Luke 12:7. This is foundational to understanding the mind of God.

The message of the sparrow is plain, personal, pertinent, and poignant. The things that man esteems as trivial, trifling, and insignificant are never overlooked under the gaze of God. Any man, endeavoring to explore the daunting depths of God, is susceptible to missing the heartbeat of the heavenly Father. For he who would dive to explore the recesses of the deep must first pass through the surface bubbles on the wave. Though one may have no interest in bubbles and has chosen to ignore them, it is the simple truths that give God His greatness. The infinite grace of our God is wrapped in the package of a common house sparrow. This must arrest our attention if we are ever to attain an ounce of His likeness.

The convergent link drawn to the worthless bird is a worthless person. There are so many things that argue for our worthlessness. While modern inventions create a larger field for man, his arrogance creeps steadily higher, and his real significance erodes. Huge corporations have been constructed to employ him. Major shopping centers clothe and feed him. Mega churches have risen to console him. And the vast world of the Internet shall educate, entertain, and engulf him with a gigantic array of options to occupy any pursuit he may imagine. In this world of accumulated intelligence, man is drowning in indescribable despair. In such a vast domain he is nothing more than a bubble on the wave drifting without purpose in the infinitude of this universe.

There was a minister who was asked by a funeral director to come and hold a funeral service. The funeral service was announced, the hour was set, the place was stated, and when the minister stood up to preach there was no one in attendance but himself and the director. While most people never experience a despondency this acute, it is real to some, and it underscores the fact that some men are esteemed of little more significance than the sparrow, yet not in the sight of God.

For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones –Isaiah 57:15. In a day when men smile and stretch their hands to receive the super-size fries, 20% more mustard in the bottle, or more footage on the roll of toilet paper… God still values the soul.

His delight is not merely in the sophisticated and prospering, but He makes His habitations among the…

…Little Ones

Such are the sparrows. The much-heralded eagles bear some disgusting traits such as feeding on dead carcasses, and we choose to overlook that they are gruesome, ravenous birds of prey. Instead, they are presented as the image of the mighty, to remind us of the glorious freedom of liberty and independence.

Children are the opposite. They are the emblem of innocence, dependance, and ignorance. And they [mothers] brought young children to him, that he [Jesus] should touch them: and his disciples rebuked those that brought them –Mark 10:13. It is rather natural for busy people to despise such little ones. For many wombs of the unborn, the life within is a cumbersome bother that is not worth the sacrifice required to retain it. Perhaps these souls, percentage wise, are the most despised humans on the face of the earth. The laws of our land have legalized the murder of them if anyone cares not for their existence. But Christ deems them otherwise. And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them –Mark 10:16.

Not only are little children despised, so likewise, are small efforts. The addition of the widow’s two mites to the treasury arrested the attention of the general populace, though not in a positive fashion. Yet God attests that her little copper coins added more to His treasury than all the noisy sacks of silver that resonated down the chute. So insignificant was the lunch provided by the lad, that the disciples declared, …but what are they among so many? –John 6:9. Despite it all, God will never miss a sparrow, and neither can He ignore the smallest sacrifice offered freely by the hands of His little ones.

…Latter Ones

Such are the sparrows. Are not the native birds of North America far superior to these newcomers? We have grown accustomed to our own preferences and traditions and have little esteem for the input of another. The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason –Proverbs 26:16. And so is the “early bird”. Folks stand for hours outside a store front in an effort to have the first chance at a bargain. These ignore the fact that their pursuit is entirely selfish, and they are driven by emotional frenzy to attain some piece of merchandise before someone else “gets it”. Life in America is offered on a “first come—first serve” basis and the thought of showing deference to another is often despised.

But this selfishness is nothing new. Christ was confronted with the same hardness when He introduced the new “wine” to the religious throng, but they insisted that the old was better. He [was] despised and rejected of men… –Isaiah 53:3, and He was deposed of at the earliest opportunity. Many will avidly spend their time in nothing else, …but either to tell, or to hear [or to purchase] some new thing. Acts 17:21, so long as it serves to gratify their curiosity or their fleshly lusts. But if that some new thing requires a sacrifice, commitment, or servanthood, it is generally destined for a sound rejection. Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: –Acts 10:34. He despises not the presence of the sparrow, nor the rude Gentile arriving at the eleventh hour under His divine surveillance.

…Lesser Ones

Such are the sparrows. An orange for the orioles, sugar water for the hummingbird, a row of cottages for the blue bird, a mansion for the martins, a suet cake for the woodpeckers… and a BB gun for the sparrows—for they are worthless. This attitude is for the birds, but it is also intricately woven into our estimation of people. Humans are considered a resource. Those that are useful are esteemed highly, but those who are not, are ignored. But God does not place His values upon human standards of excellence. The rich and poor meet together: the LORD is the maker of them all –Proverbs 22:2.

Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom … But ye have despised the poor… James 2:5-6. Herein lies the difference in the eyes of the beholder. A cup of cold water given in charity will not go unnoticed by God. Neither will the praise of a sparrow.

The totalitarian governments of communist regimes have been blatant offenders. Any human who could not or would not contribute to the furtherance of the political vision was exterminated. In our western society, we sigh and lament at the vast ignorance and injustice of such prejudice precinct, while our own nursing homes are full of discarded souls that are regarded as worthless and unworthy of our time and attention. We are too busy for our children and too busy for our parents, but the God who watches every sparrow fall esteems the lesser ones of much greater value than we do.

…Lackluster Ones

Such are the sparrows. The robin boasts his red breast and the cardinal his red crest, but the sparrow is drab brown. We have an innate insistence for beauty. If our hair is gray, it must be dyed. If our teeth are crooked, they must be straightened. If our car has rust, it must be replaced. Most are infernally infatuated with that which is beautiful. Beauty is in the eyes of the beholder, and our God looks far past the surface. …let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price –1 Peter 3:3-4. Many will go to extra efforts to deplete their outward ostentation but forget that the emphasis of the verse is to make the inner heart beautiful.

God obviously has no qualms with physical beauty. He paints the sky with golden hues and adorns the rose in scarlet. But there are also sparrows that lack the splendor to attract human appreciation that do not go unnoticed by God. So are the anonymous earth dwellers who can do no more than weep at the feet of their Lord and wipe His dirty feet with their hair. These despised “sparrows” are royal diadems in the crown of Christ.

…Lost Ones

The woman who lost her silver searched her house until it was found, likewise, the shepherd with his lost lamb. But the search was made based upon the perceived value placed upon the lost item. Society is brimming over with an overabundance of lost souls. Not just lost to the salvation plan of God, but totally clueless to the laws of happiness. Perhaps, like the sparrows, they are overlooked because there are so many of them. At times, some caring souls venture from the beaten path of common words to help them, but soon retreat when attempts prove too meager to improve their condition. Despite it all, these misfits are noticed by God and their value is far above the sparrows.

While some will thrust all their evangelical energies toward the lost heathen on foreign soils, there is another lost entity here on our own turf. This is a lost respect and appreciation for the local church. Para-church Outreaches, personal ministries, retreats, and seminars lend an exciting appeal, to religious zealots, while the weekly meetings in the local church seem rather common and drab. While man runs from shore to shore to find his lost inspiration, Christ asks …Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth? –Luke 18:8.

…Two farthings

The encouraging dimension of this comparison is that sparrows are relatively easy to obtain: For ye have the poor with you always, and whensoever ye will ye may do them good… –Mark 14:7. And a farthing is not a major expenditure. The only thing we must do is adjust our value system. If we wonder what we value most, we need not look farther than our own farthings. The avenues of life that reach out to receive our copper coins are the shrines that hold our hands and our hearts: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also –Matthew 6:21. Once our heart is open, our hands are sure to follow. For us, the fifth sparrow is somebody in need for whom Christ died. The great destiny and the call of the church is to extend a sensitive heart and a saving hand to the despised and neglected of our land. At the arrival of every humble sacrifice laid on the counter, God’s ready smile imparts the fifth sparrow for free.

Why do trees along the river,
Lean so far out o’er the tide?
Very wise men tell me why,
But I am never satisfied.

And so I keep my fancy still,
That trees lean out to save
The drowning from the clutches of
The cold remorseless wave.

–Alex Posey

Alex Posey – 1873-1908, a Creek Indian poet, died when he was trying to help two white people across the flooded North Canadian River. He held onto a branch of a tree until help came, but by the time they could throw him a rope his hands had paralyzed, and he couldn’t unmold them to clasp the rope, so he sank out of sight beneath the waters and died in the tide.
